A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LogicAgent and RepublicQA study. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison; relocated content can be matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations in Section 5, plus dataset analyses, error analyses, and computational measurements in Appendices D–G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, dataset analyses, error analyses, and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendices D–G.

M1.justification: The three-stage LogicAgent pipeline, semiotic-square construction and validation, Translator/Planner/Solver components, reflection procedures, and Appendix H prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same logical-reasoning coverage: RepublicQA, ProntoQA, ProofWriter, FOLIO, and ProverQA. No dataset, domain, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same seven evaluated comparators: Naive Prompting, CoT, CR, ToT, Logic-LM, SymbCoT, and Aristotle. Their participation across the reported benchmarks is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same dataset splits, including ProntoQA 5-hop, ProofWriter depth-5 under OWA, and ProverQA's 500-example hard split. Model assignments, temperature zero, metrics, and ablation and efficiency procedures also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the component and input-modality ablations, runtime comparisons, and semantic-complexity versus hop-depth analysis in Section 5.3. The appendix case study, error analyses, and token/stage-cost analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the mean/median token summaries in Table 8 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4, 6, 8–9 and the result figures retain the same values and findings. For example, Table 2 reports RepublicQA accuracies of 82.50 with Qwen2.5 and 87.00 with GPT-4o in both versions; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its proof, the existential import definition, Lemma 1, Table 1's construction rules, the decision equations, and Appendix B's formal grammar are unchanged beyond typesetting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: semiotic-guided multi-perspective reasoning, RepublicQA's joint semantic and logical complexity, superior benchmark performance, and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic ambiguity and complementary natural-language/FOL inputs remain unchanged. Section 5.3 and Appendix F retain the same limitations concerning excessive planning depth, translation-error propagation, difficulty constructing contraries, and inconsistent verification.

D1.justification: v5's abstract adds an explicit code-availability statement and a link to the AI4SS/Logic-Agent repository. v3 only describes partial submission materials and a future full release. Those release statements remain in v5, so the PDFs establish improved access information without establishing repository completeness.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds citations to Feng et al. (2025a), Efficient Reasoning Models: A Survey, and Feng et al. (2025b), Can MLLMs Guide Me Home?, with corresponding references. The surrounding discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The author block adds Yi-Ping Phoebe Chen and the La Trobe University affiliation, and the abstract gains a code-access sentence. Beyond these limited textual additions and citations, the prose and section organization remain essentially identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 move from pages 1 and 2 to pages 2 and 3. Figure 5 moves below the continuing planning discussion on page 9, with associated text reflow. Figure content, captions, and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 improves documented code access through an explicit repository link and modestly improves reading flow, particularly by placing Figure 5 after the planning discussion. These are limited practical gains; the scientific evidence is unchanged, and the retained future-release statement leaves full code and data availability unconfirmed by the PDFs.
